items.title: Cadence Design Systems (CDNS) Stock Still Looks Overvalued Despite AI Chip Demand
items.summary: Cadence Design Systems stock has pulled back in recent months, yet the latest valuation checks still point to a rich price tag, with both the market multiple view and an intrinsic value estimate suggesting the shares trade at a premium. At the same time, the company continues to push its technology forward in areas such as PCIe 6.0, which helps explain why investors are willing to pay up. items.title: Cadence Design Systems (CDNS) Following PCIe 6.0 Progress Has Fair Value Back In Focus
items.summary: Cadence Design Systems (CDNS) recently reported first pass compliance for its PCIe 6.0 PHY and controller IP on TSMC’s N3 process, which has put a fresh spotlight on the stock after a weaker year of returns. Despite the PCIe 6.0 milestone, Cadence Design Systems’ recent share price performance has been weak, with the stock down 22.19% over 90 days and 13.16% over 30 days. items.title: What Sets Cadence Design Systems (CDNS) Apart After Its PCIe 6.0 Milestone?
items.summary: Cadence Design Systems (NasdaqGS: CDNS) reported that its PCIe 6.0 subsystem achieved first pass compliance at an official PCI-SIG workshop and is now listed on the PCI-SIG Integrators List. The production ready subsystem targets high bandwidth connectivity needs in AI and high performance computing markets. items.title: Synopsys Fell 11% This Year. Wall Street Expects It to Gain 50% in the Next 12 Months
items.summary: Synopsys powers nearly every advanced chip on the planet, yet its stock has cratered while the broader market surged, and Wall Street analysts are betting that gap closes in a hurry.

items.title: Synopsys' Core Engine Grew Far Slower Than Its Revenue
items.summary: Synopsys (SNPS) booked revenue of $2.477 billion in fiscal Q3 2026, up about 42% year over year, and the shares have still lost about 30% over the past twelve months. Look past that headline at the line underneath it: EDA grew 8.5%. That single-digit number is the pace of the design tools business Synopsys had before the Ansys deal.
